svg.text: LCFS pushed FIRST — stationary points & limited/diverted class emerge after
1 · Field ψ(R,Z)
harmonic plasma + thick-cylinder coil flux; the near-pole
interior TH-null "garbage" disk is masked & excluded.
2 · Push the LCFS outward
from the axis, STARTING OUTSIDE the garbage: sweep the
flux offset outward, tracing the axis-enclosing contour
(contourpy) at each level.
3 · LCFS = outermost closed ring
the largest ring that ENCLOSES the axis AND fits inside
the limiter. Continuous across the transition.
ONE code path. No class needed to find it.
4 · Stationary points + class EMERGE
now the boundary is known: find ∇ψ=0 points;
X-point ON the boundary ring → diverted (report it);
boundary on the wall, no near X-point → limited.
A soft read-off by proximity — never a code switch.
The loop is reversed
A classifier asks “is there an X-point on the
boundary?” FIRST — but limited↔diverted is a
CONTINUOUS transition: just-limited and just-
diverted look identical, so the discrete class is
ill-posed exactly where it would matter. Chasing
it (wall contacts, ψ-extrema on limiter surfaces)
is the EFIT-extractor trap.
Instead we track the CONTINUOUS quantity — the
boundary SHAPE — which is well-posed across the
transition, in one contour push (step 3).
The stationary points & the class then fall out
as DIAGNOSTICS (step 4), by X-point proximity to
the known boundary. Near the transition the class
is softly undefined — as the physics demands — and
the LCFS shape is unaffected. No topology extractor.
